Performers
Bramwell Tovey (piano), United States Marine Band (ensemble) Documented

Tovey is credited as the Rhapsody’s piano soloist. Although he is the gala’s guest conductor, the consulted recording metadata does not separately identify who conducts this work; no work-specific conductor credit or individual band-player roster is supplied here.

[1] [2]
Work version
Ferde Grofé’s original 1924 jazz-band orchestration, performed by Bramwell Tovey and the United States Marine Band Documented

The Marine Band’s concert announcement and the recording description both specify the 1924 jazz-band version. The score edition, reconstructed parts and any small performance alterations are not identified. This is one continuous concert performance, not a joining of the 1924 disc sides. Formal boundaries are passage-level editorial estimates; the long third section groups the broad melody, its piano continuation and the finale before the closing reprise. No bar alignment or aural review is asserted.

[1] [2] [3]
Recorded
2018-07-10 Documented

Live 220th-anniversary gala, corroborated by the recording description and the official concert announcement.

[1] [2]
Place
The Music Center at Strathmore, North Bethesda, Maryland, United States Documented

Venue stated by both sources. The recording equipment and microphone positions are not documented.

[1] [2]
Label
United States Marine Band — online concert publication Documented

Institutional publication, not a commercial record-label attribution. The official announcement states that the gala will stream on the Marine Band’s website and YouTube channel.

[1] [2]
Transfer
United States Marine Band, recording publisher; Mysterymanblue, Wikimedia Commons uploader Documented

The host identifies the band as author and Mysterymanblue as uploader. Individual recording, editing and mastering engineers are unknown.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

Commons first received the audio on 2 January 2021; the current revision was uploaded on 6 February 2021. Those dates document file publication, not the date on which the source soundtrack was extracted or mastered.

[1]
Processing
Ogg Vorbis audio from the concert video, followed by a Wikimedia MP3 access derivative; a few leading seconds of silence removed in the current Commons revision Documented

The 6 February 2021 upload comment states ‘Higher bitrate (from the original); removed few seconds of silence at the beginning’. Commons lists an MP3 transcode completed on 25 February 2026. Original recording resolution, microphone chain, mixing, equalisation, compression and further processing are undocumented. The source video’s timestamps therefore are not copied to the audio’s listening notes.

[1]
Composition rights
Public domain in the United States: Gershwin’s 1924 composition and Grofé’s 1924 jazz-band orchestration Documented

IMSLP explicitly identifies the original jazz-band setting as public domain in the United States while warning that Grofé’s orchestrations remain protected in many other countries. This is a territorial US assessment of the specified original setting, not clearance of the 1942 symphonic orchestration, unidentified modern editorial additions, or all territories.

[3] [1]
Recording rights
Public domain in the United States under the host’s PD-USGov-⁠Military-⁠Marine Corps designation Documented

Commons separately marks the performance/recording as a work made by a United States Marine or employee in official duties. The supplied file is accepted on that explicit host designation, not merely on the ensemble’s name. The statutory US-government-work rule is territorial; no worldwide public-domain status is asserted, and the guest soloist’s contractual documents are not published in the consulted sources.

[1] [4]

George Gershwin, Rhapsody in Blue, orchestrated by Ferde Grofé (1924 jazz-band version). Bramwell Tovey, piano; United States Marine Band. The Music Center at Strathmore, 10 July 2018. Audio supplied by Wikimedia Commons, uploaded by Mysterymanblue; public domain in the United States under the host’s US-government-work designation. Rights statement

Performance/Recording licence template PD-USGov-⁠Military-⁠Marine Corps; current upload history and leading-silence edit; MP3 transcode; duration 1089.72158333333 seconds. The source video’s oEmbed endpoint returned HTTP 403 during research, so no independently checked oEmbed author is asserted.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  2. United States Marine Band — U.S. Marine Band Celebrates 220th Anniversary with Bramwell Tovey — Master Sgt. Kristin duBois, 6 July 2018. Official programme announcement: 10 July, Strathmore; Tovey as pianist in the 1924 jazz-band Rhapsody; planned Marine Band website and channel livestream. Opened and read in a browser after the static reader received HTTP 403.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  3. IMSLP — Rhapsody in Blue work and territorial-rights information — General Information: original jazz-band instrumentation; first publication of the two-piano score in 1924; US-public-domain status of the 1924 and 1926 Grofé versions, distinct from the later symphonic orchestration and other territories.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  4. 17 USC 105 — United States Government works — Subsection (a) and Historical and Revision Notes: works prepared by US officers or employees in official duties; distinction from private contractors and copyright outside the United States.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  5. Jim Farrington — Rhapsody in Blue, National Recording Registry essay — pp. 1–⁠2: original scoring and première, the opening clarinet glissando, and the shortened 1924 acoustic record. The essay concerns the historical record, not this 2018 performance.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  6. David Schiff — Gershwin: Rhapsody in Blue, Cambridge University Press excerpt — Printed pp. 4–⁠10 inspected as images. Original instrumentation, p. 5; Table 1, pp. 7–⁠9, gives thematic sequence, cadenzas, broad melody and closing ritornello, with the 1924 recording’s cuts in column G. This is a structural source, not an alignment to Tovey’s recording.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  7. Rhapsody in Blue — formal and tonal analysis — Form and analysis: opening and ending in B-flat major, blues-inflected melodic writing, train theme, and the piano styles. No million-selling claim is adopted.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
